verdict.rationale: Speech is Cheap runs its own hosted MCP server that, per its docs, "lets AI assistants transcribe audio and video files directly within your conversations." That server exposes job-operation tools (cancel_job, prepare_upload, check_access) and the prompt templates "transcribe" and "subtitles", and a runtime probe confirms the endpoint is live and OAuth-gated. So users can drive the product through natural-language conversation. The language understanding itself comes from the user's external AI client, though, and there is no hands-on proof of a conversational session. Missing for 10: a native natural-language interface in the product itself, independent or hands-on corroboration of end-to-end conversational operation, and a complete enumeration of the MCP tools covering every job action.
